To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
extracellular ATP induces the rapid loss of CD 23 from human DC by activating P2X7 purinergic receptors.
ATP-induced shedding of the B lymphocyte marker CD23 is a rapid and early event in the activation of monocyte-derived DC.
ATP induces a near complete loss of CD23 within 2 min from the surface of DC via activation of P(2X7) receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ATP in regulating the immune system.
the role of P2X receptor activation in the regulation of DC maturation and function.
the role of ATP as an extracellular signaling molecule.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loss of CD23 expression from human DC is a rapid consequence of P2X receptor activation.
P2X7 is a key player in dendritic cell biology, which may have implications in a variety of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.

the P2X(7) receptor is a key player in the control of DC maturation, and that its activation by extracellular ATP may be an important mechanism in the control of the DC response to infection and/or inflammation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATP-induced shedding of cell surface molecules is not a general feature of P2X receptor activation in all cell types.
P2X7 activation on monocyte derived dendritic cells leads to the rapid and complete loss of CD23 via activation of a membrane metalloproteinase.
ATP induces a loss of the B cell co-stimulatory molecule, CD23, from DC, and this effect is mediated by the P2X(7) receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ATP induces the rapid and near complete loss of CD23, and this loss is mediated by activation of P2 receptors, including P2X7, on the surface of human DC.

ATP can induce rapid and near complete loss of CD23 expression on monocyte-derived dendritic cells via the activation of P2 receptors, and that the rapid loss of CD2 is impaired on dendritic cells from individuals who are homozyggous for a loss of function polymorphism in the P2X receptor gene.
ATP is a novel sheddase for CD23 on DC and that this shedding is mediated via P2X7R.
